Thanks again for the intro call this morning. To move procurement forward we need a short, concrete sizing recommendation from Redwood for our private VPC pool. High level asks below: 

- Sustained inference throughput target: 1200 concurrent requests (avg request = 350 tokens) with 95th p99 latency target <= 450ms for chat requests.
- Bursting behavior: support 3x the sustained (burst to 3600 concurrent) for windows up to 2 minutes.
- Egress: we will route model artifacts and manage logs through our NAT/egress gateway — need to ensure per-node egress and peering constraints are acceptable.
- Timeline: we want a pilot by late June and GA by September.

Please include assumptions around batching, KV cache warmup, and any recommended headroom (safety margin) and network topology (VPC peering, NAT throughput). Also call out any hardware-family recommendations (A100 vs H100/8-bit) and quantization tradeoffs.

Can you shoot over an initial recommendation today/tomorrow? We are prepping our procurement packet.

Diego — quick notes inline per your asks.

- GPU family sizing:
  - H100 (FP16) baseline: 20 cards to hit sustained 1200 conc at 450ms 95th, assuming 75% chat and average per-request token footprint 350 tokens. This assumes continuous batching window 15ms and KV-cache warm (50% hit rate).
  - A100 (FP16): ~28 cards for same targets.
  - Quantized (int8/8-bit): ~14–16 H100-equivalents (depends on model accuracy checks) — call this a risk tradeoff for procurement.

- Headroom: recommend 25% safety margin for sustained, and reserve an additional 40% on demand as pre-warmed burst pool (separate allocation) to hit 3x for up to 2 minutes without cold starts. Practically: provision 25 H100-equivalents for sustained + 10-card warm burst pool.

- Runtime assumptions: batching window: 15ms for chat steering; avg token throughput per GPU = ~45 kTok/s in these conditions; KV-cache hit = 50%; model = 70B-class recommended.

Diego/Marissa —

Network notes for Oríon: 

- Egress requirements: to sustain 3x bursts across the VPC we need end-to-end egress provision of ~120Gbps aggregated across the subnets that host the GPU nodes (rough calc: 3600 conc * avg 350 tokens * ~1.1 bytes/token + protocol overhead). If Oríon NAT is limited to 40Gbps/subnet they should provision multiple NAT gateways (3+) or use a transit peering with multi-path egress.
- Per-node: recommend 100Gbps NICs on GPU hosts; use SR-IOV and mtu 9000 for lower CPU overhead.
- Topology: Active/Active peering to Redwood private ingress (if they plan to pull model caches) + local egress for logs. Provide a small failover path to a secondary NAT in a different AZ with stateful failover scripts.
- NAT saturation failure mode: if nat is saturated we see TCP stalls and queueing at the host which increases p99 beyond 1s within 30–90s — recommended mitigation: admission-control gates at 1.5x sustained (i.e., refuse new sessions beyond 1800 conc) and prefer shedding low-priority batch/async work first.

I'll attach a diagram (egress_topology_v2.png) and a short `sysctl`/iptables snippet for their ops team.

—Jonas

Simon —

Thanks for the ask. Short summary and next steps attached. Key recommendation highlights: 

- Sustained configuration: 25 H100-equivalent cards (H100 preferred) sized to meet 1.2k concurrent with 25% safety headroom. Runtime defaults: 15ms batching window, KV-cache targeted 50% hit rate.
- Burst handling: pre-warm a 10-card warm pool to support 3x bursts for up to 2 minutes without cold-starts. Combine this with admission control (see thresholds below).
- Network topology: Oríon should provision multi-NAT per-subnet or a transit peering to achieve ~120Gbps aggregated egress. Per-node: 100Gbps NICs + MTU 9000. If NAT cannot be scaled, use an active/active peering model and replicate small model artifacts locally to reduce egress during bursts.
- Autoscale gates: recommended thresholds — soft-queue at 1.25x sustained (1500 conc), hard-reject at 1.5x (1800 conc). For bursts above hard-reject, shed low-priority/async batch traffic and route premium chat to the warm pool.

I've attached two files: orion_capacity_model_v1.xlsx (capacity math + sensitivity table) and egress_topology_v2.png (diagram + iptables snippets). Links and a one-pager are in Drive: https://drive.redwood.com/open?id=orion-capacity-v1 (see HS-78321).

If this looks good I can convert the workbook figures into procurement-friendly language and join your procurement call tomorrow.

Best,
